trajectory_summary: The call opens cleanly with a cooperative customer moving through address, roof type, and roof age with no friction. It ends abruptly when the rep, on a single 'no' to a tree-removal question, declares the home disqualified in the same breath rather than exploring the shading situation further or handing off to the design/specialist team. The customer, previously compliant, shuts the call down within seconds.
outcome_dispute: V1 tag is unknown/unclear; observed outcome here is a DQ, but it is a rep-declared DQ delivered as a flat, one-line rule rather than an escalation or investigation. Whether 'has trees in the way, unwilling to remove' is a genuine hard DQ or something the design team should still evaluate (e.g., partial shading, panel placement away from the wooded area) is unresolved operational truth — TBD with Kenny — not a settled fact this transcript can confirm either way.

observed_outcome.quote: Okay. Well, realistically speaking, solar wouldn't be a good option for your home unless you remove the trees you have in the way.
observed_outcome.reasoning: The rep explicitly disqualifies the home due to tree shading and the customer confirms she will not remove the trees, ending the call with no appointment set.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The call was ended at the roof/tree qualifier stage before the rep reached utility company or bill amount questions in the verify sequence.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep confirmed the customer had submitted a solar request ('Does that ring a bell?') but never asked what specifically interested her in solar; the call was disqualified before this beat was reached.

script_coverage.quote: This is Corey with Ion. I'm just reaching out because I got a request that you're looking at solar for your home.
You gave us 3776 Fallen Tree Lane in Cincinnati, Ohio. Is that correct?
Is that an asphalt shingle roof?

primary_coaching_focus.topic: single-answer disqualification without escalation or follow-up
primary_coaching_focus.quote: Okay. Well, realistically speaking, solar wouldn't be a good option for your home unless you remove the trees you have in the way. So I would recommend removing the trees you have in the backyard before doing solar.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The rep ends a fully cooperative call on one yes/no answer with no clarifying follow-up (tree height, location, distance from roof) and no attempt to route to the design team for an actual shading assessment. Whether this is trained policy or freelanced judgment is unresolved and should be checked with Kenny first, but either way the rep needed a follow-up question and a softer, non-final framing before closing the door.

key_moments.quote: Yeah. I replaced it. Maybe ten years. I don't know. I replaced it, but I don't remember when. Let's say ten years.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer gives a visibly hedged, low-confidence estimate on roof age — a DQ-adjacent field (roof_age_over_15_no_replacement_planned) — and the rep logs it at face value with a flat 'Perfect' rather than noting the uncertainty or gently confirming.

key_moments.quote: Okay. Well, realistically speaking, solar wouldn't be a good option for your home unless you remove the trees you have in the way. So I would recommend removing the trees you have in the backyard before doing solar.
key_moments.stewart_read: This reads as a genuine toss-up between two hypotheses: (1) the rep is reciting a trained, formulaic DQ rule verbatim in response to a single yes/no answer, or (2) the rep is freelancing a technical judgment about shading that belongs to the design/specialist team. The flat, rehearsed cadence ('realistically speaking... I would recommend') supports the trained-rule reading as much as the freelance reading, and the coaching prescription differs materially between the two.

key_moments.quote: And then have you had any trees in the backyard removed?
key_moments.stewart_read: This single closed-ended question is used as the sole gate for an entire appointment decision — a verify-question-design gap, not a curiosity/features issue. The rep asks a yes/no question and treats a 'no' as sufficient to end the call without exploring degree of shading, tree location, or possible panel placement.
